title: Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average Greater than or Equal to Threshold

constraints.meaning: Up to 100,000 elements. The window length k is at least 1 and never longer than the array.
constraints.impact: Summing every window from scratch is O(n·k), up to about 10¹⁰ steps when k is near n/2: too slow. You need O(n). There is always at least one full window.

constraints.meaning: Every value is positive and at most 10,000.
constraints.impact: A window sum is at most 10⁵ × 10⁴ = 10⁹, so int is enough.

constraints.meaning: The threshold is a whole number, at most 10,000.
constraints.impact: average ≥ threshold is the same as sum ≥ threshold × k. That needs no division and no doubles, and threshold × k ≤ 10⁹ still fits in int. With threshold = 0 every window counts.

bruteForce.summary: for every start i, add up arr[i..i+k-1] from scratch, compute the average and count it when it is ≥ threshold. O(n·k) time, which is too slow when n = 10⁵ and k is large.

examples.label: Average exactly equal, k = n: [4,4,4], k = 3, threshold = 4
